records.name: Policy definition and immutable platform binding
records.summary: A Relution policy is a collection of one or more configurations that can apply to one or more devices; a device can have multiple policies, and the platform selected when the policy is created cannot later be changed.
capabilities: Collect one or more configurations in one policy definition
Associate one policy with multiple devices and multiple policies with one device
Bind a policy at creation to exactly one platform family

Confirm the target release exposes every required configuration type
Define the organization, intended device audience, and ownership
Plan publication, assignment, verification, and rollback as separate stages

scope.organization_behavior: Ordinary policies belong to an organization; global policies have separate cross-organization semantics and must not be treated as ordinary organization policy copies.

reasons: A published and assigned policy can change security, network, identity, application, and device behavior
The platform choice is immutable
One definition may reach many devices through group assignment
risk.blast_radius: One unpublished definition during editing, or every device reached by its assignments after publication.

required_for: Changes to security, trust, network, identity, application, or destructive configuration

effects: Create, edit, publish, restore, assign, prioritize, deactivate, reactivate, or delete policy state
external_effects: Published assignments deliver configuration to managed devices
destructive_effects: Deletion or restrictive configuration can remove access, applications, profiles, certificates, or connectivity depending on the selected platform schema
concurrency_cautions: Do not edit, publish, and assign as one opaque operation
Re-read template, published version, priority, assignments, and revision controls before each bounded mutation

stop_conditions: Target schema differs from the plan
Published or assigned state changes concurrently

requirements: Capture the prior published version, priority, assignment set, and device-specific activation state
Prepare a new policy if the selected platform was wrong
Retain a known-good connectivity baseline
limitations: The platform of an existing policy cannot be changed
Device-side effects may require check-in, a compensating configuration, or manual recovery

Confirm immutable platform fields and replacement-versus-patch semantics

records.name: Device policy application status
records.summary: Relution reports seven distinct device policy states; they describe assignment and device convergence and must not be reduced to a Boolean success value.
capabilities: UNKNOWN: the status of the device policy is unknown
NONE: no policy is applied to the device
SENT: a policy is assigned but has not yet been applied
APPLIED: the policy is being applied and is shown as Active
UPDATE: a new policy version was sent but the device has not yet updated it
CHANGE: another policy was sent but the device has not yet changed policy
REMOVED: the policy was unassigned but the device has not yet removed it
Distinguish accepted assignment from terminal functional verification
prerequisites: Resolve the exact device, policy, assignment, and expected version
Confirm inventory freshness and device check-in health
Use the target contract for the exact wire representation

scope.organization_behavior: Status is observed per device and policy context; aggregate fleet status must preserve each device result rather than generalize from one sample.

reasons: Misreading SENT, UPDATE, CHANGE, or REMOVED as complete can produce false assurance
UNKNOWN can conceal device or delivery problems
risk.blast_radius: One incorrectly interpreted device result or an entire rollout if aggregate status is collapsed.

required_for: Separate explicit approval for any action intended to change status

effects: This registry models observation; assignment, publication, refresh, and device check-in operations cause status transitions
concurrency_cautions: Status may change asynchronously between reads
Preserve per-device observations and timestamps

preconditions: Know the intended policy version and assignment state
read_back: Read status until the target-documented terminal expectation is reached without unbounded polling
Verify the affected configuration independently on the device where authorized
audit: Correlate preceding publication, assignment, refresh, or removal events
functional_checks: Confirm the intended device behavior instead of treating a status label alone as proof
stop_conditions: SENT, UPDATE, CHANGE, or REMOVED does not converge within the agreed window

requirements: Rollback the causal publication or assignment operation, not the observed status value
limitations: Status is evidence, not a directly editable desired-state field

contract_checks: Confirm the exact target enum and casing

Identify timestamps and device check-in fields needed to evaluate freshness

evidence.claim: Relution documents exactly the policy states UNKNOWN, NONE, SENT, APPLIED, UPDATE, CHANGE, and REMOVED with distinct meanings.

Preserve recovery keys and a secondary administrator path
Map all higher-precedence policies that may override or complement the change

scope.organization_behavior: Policy configuration is organization-scoped, while conditional-access and compliance results can affect access to connected external services.

reasons: Restrictions and access rules can lock out users or devices
Encryption mistakes can cause data-recovery loss
Compliance changes can trigger dynamic group and external access effects
risk.blast_radius: One pilot or all devices, users, and external access paths reached by the effective policy.

required_for: Password, lock, restriction, encryption, compliance, update, or conditional-access changes

effects: Change device restrictions, security, encryption, update, compliance, and access posture
external_effects: May allow or deny connected-service access and trigger dynamic membership
destructive_effects: Can lock users out, remove permitted functions, or make encrypted data unrecoverable
concurrency_cautions: Preserve recovery access
Account for policy priority and dynamic-group feedback
Coordinate updates and restarts

preconditions: Capture current effective policy, compliance, encryption, access, and group state
Retain tested recovery credentials and keys
read_back: Read policy version, assignment, device status, compliance state, and external access decision independently
audit: Match policy, compliance, access, and assignment events
functional_checks: Test required and denied behavior on one approved pilot and identity
stop_conditions: Device enters an unexpected dynamic group

requirements: Retain prior published version, recovery keys, compliance rules, and group/access mappings
Prepare compensating external-access and encryption actions
limitations: Encryption and external access consequences may not reverse immediately
Lost credentials or data cannot be recreated by republishing

contract_checks: Inspect precedence and platform applicability
Identify recovery, encryption, and write-only fields
Separate policy configuration from observed compliance and external-access state

evidence.claim: Relution's official platform policy indexes document passcode/password, restrictions, app conformance, conditional access, updates, FileVault, security, and BitLocker configurations.

records.name: Content, media, display, and files domain
records.summary: This domain covers configurations for managed files and media, fonts, wallpapers, web links, content filtering, display layout, AirPlay, conference-room presentation, and related user-facing content.
capabilities: Configure fonts, wallpaper, managed media, files, and web links
Configure homescreen, desktop, Dock, Finder, screensaver, and conference-room presentation behavior where supported
Configure content and URL filtering
Configure AirPlay and display-related behavior
Configure managed files or content applications
prerequisites: Review content provenance, copyright, integrity, and sensitivity
Confirm target platform, storage capacity, network delivery, and application dependency
Freeze exact file, media, URL, font, or display resources

scope.organization_behavior: Content definitions and policies belong to an organization, while referenced URLs, files, or streaming services may be external.

reasons: Content filters can block required services
Large or sensitive content can create privacy, storage, and bandwidth impact
Shared displays can expose unintended information
risk.blast_radius: One content item or every assigned device, user, display, and network path.

required_for: Upload, publication, assignment, replacement, or deletion of managed content
Content-filter, wallpaper, display, AirPlay, or external URL changes

effects: Change managed content, display, filter, file, media, font, wallpaper, and link configuration
external_effects: Downloads content, contacts referenced services, and changes shared displays
destructive_effects: Filters can remove access to critical services
concurrency_cautions: Pin resource identity or hash
Account for bandwidth and storage
Coordinate room and display usage

preconditions: Confirm content hash, source, destination, size, privacy, and exact audience
Identify required URLs that must remain reachable
read_back: Read policy payload, resource metadata, assignment, download/application status, and policy status
audit: Match content upload, policy publication, assignment, and deletion events
functional_checks: Open or render the content and test required/blocked URLs on one approved pilot
stop_conditions: Content provenance or audience is unclear
Sensitive content appears on an unintended display

requirements: Retain prior policy version and content resource
Prepare re-upload or re-assignment
Preserve required URL allowlists
limitations: Already displayed or downloaded content cannot be recalled reliably
Deleted content may require recovery from the source

contract_checks: Separate resource upload/reference operations from policy configuration
Inspect hashes, media types, limits, and URL validation
Identify deletion and device-removal behavior

evidence.claim: Relution's official platform policy indexes document fonts, wallpaper, managed media, files, content filters, web links, AirPlay, and conference-room configuration families.

records.name: Identity, accounts, certificates, mail, and network domain
records.summary: This domain covers configurations for identity and account binding, SSO, certificates, directory and mail accounts, Wi-Fi, VPN, proxies, DNS, Ethernet, radio controls, and related trust paths.
capabilities: Configure SSO, accounts, login, Active Directory, work-account, and shared-user behavior where supported
Configure email, Exchange, calendars, contacts, and administered domains
Configure certificates, SCEP, and platform trust payloads
Configure Wi-Fi, VPN, per-app VPN, Ethernet, HTTP proxy, DNS proxy, DNS encryption, and content-network controls
Configure Android radio state and supported network behavior
prerequisites: Retain a tested out-of-band administrator and management-connectivity path
Resolve certificate ownership, expiry, chain, and private-key handling
Validate Wi-Fi, VPN, proxy, DNS, directory, mail, and identity endpoints
Confirm platform and enrollment applicability
sensitive_value_classes: Directory, SSO, mail, proxy, and network configuration

scope.organization_behavior: Policy payloads are organization-scoped but connect managed devices and users to external identity, certificate, network, and mail services.

reasons: A bad network or trust payload can sever MDM connectivity
Identity and certificate changes can lock out users or expose credentials
Mail and VPN changes affect external services
risk.blast_radius: One pilot or every assigned device, user, certificate trust path, and connected service.

required_for: SSO, account, certificate, Wi-Fi, VPN, proxy, DNS, directory, Exchange, mail, or radio changes

effects: Change device identity, trust, account, mail, and network configuration
external_effects: Authenticates to and exchanges data with identity, certificate, network, VPN, and mail services
destructive_effects: Certificate removal, credential replacement, or network changes can cause lockout and management loss
concurrency_cautions: Stage new trust before removing old trust where supported
Never publish a Wi-Fi replacement without a tested baseline path
Coordinate external provider changes

preconditions: Confirm endpoint names, certificate chain and expiry, credential source, network reachability, and recovery path
Capture current effective network and identity payloads
read_back: Read policy version, assignment, policy status, safe metadata, and connected-service status without exposing secrets
audit: Match policy, certificate, identity, mail, and network events
functional_checks: Test management check-in, login, certificate trust, Wi-Fi/VPN, and approved mail behavior on one pilot
stop_conditions: Certificate ownership or endpoint identity is unclear
Pilot loses MDM, network, login, VPN, or mail access

requirements: Capture prior non-secret state and retain approved prior trust/credential material
Prepare forward certificate rotation and network recovery
Keep a known-good baseline connectivity policy
limitations: Expired or revoked trust cannot be restored by replay alone
A disconnected device may require local intervention before receiving rollback

contract_checks: Inspect write-only secret and certificate-reference fields
Confirm replacement-versus-merge behavior and trust overlap
Separate policy payload from provider settings and connectivity tests

evidence.claim: Relution's official macOS policy overview lists directory, SSO, accounts, mail, certificates, SCEP, Wi-Fi, VPN, proxy, DNS, and Ethernet configurations.
The Android Enterprise policy overview documents work-account and device-radio configuration families alongside security and application controls.
